companyDescription: Dividend-quality ETF — tracks Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100: 100 high-quality, high-yield US companies. Low cost, ~3.3% yield, value tilt.

summary: SCHD is the top DCA fund pick: a low-cost (0.06%) dividend-quality ETF yielding ~3.3% with a value tilt that screens cheaper than the broad market. Built-in quality screens (profitability, cash flow, dividend growth) make it an ideal hands-off monthly accumulation vehicle.

catalysts.name: Quarterly dividend compounding
catalysts.description: Reinvested ~3.3% yield + dividend growth compounds steadily over years.

risks: Value/dividend tilt can lag in a growth-led bull market
Sector reconstitution risk at annual index rebalance
Rising rates make the yield relatively less attractive

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Dividend payers can wobble when rates spike, but quality screen limits damage.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Dividend growers historically outpace inflation over time.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Value/quality tilt is defensive vs a tech-led drawdown.
macroRisk.summary: Low Fed sensitivity and a defensive quality-value tilt — the steadiest DCA fund in the list.

valuationBand.basis: Value/dividend tilt trades at a lower index P/E than the broad market; price near 52-wk midpoint ($26.2–32.9)

qualityScore.note: 100 quality dividend names (diversification), 0.06% cost, reliable ~3.3% yield, $96B AUM / Schwab.

dcaPlan.note: DCA monthly and reinvest dividends (DRIP) — the income-compounding anchor of the basket.

technicalNote.note: Trading near the upper half of its 52-week range, above the 200-DMA — steady uptrend.

thesisBreak: Expense ratio materially raised or fund wound down
Index methodology change that abandons the quality/dividend screen
Structural, multi-year underperformance vs the broad market beyond the normal value cycle

stopLoss.rrNote: DCA + DRIP, not a daily stop

entryStrategy.verdict: Top DCA fund — low-cost dividend quality at a fair price. Accumulate monthly + DRIP.
